devdoc.details: Only proof hashes (bytes32) are stored on-chain. The full Reclaim JSON proof lives off-chain (IPFS/Arweave) and is verified off-chain. Trust model for `isVerified`, strongest to weakest:   1. On-chain verified (trustless): {submitVerifiedProof} passes the full      Reclaim proof to a deployed Reclaim verifier ({reclaimVerifier}) which      checks the witness signatures on-chain. Verification accrues to the      proof's `owner` (the address the proof was issued to), so a valid proof      cannot be replayed to verify a different account. This is the production      path and gives `isVerified` cryptographic meaning with no trusted party.   2. Attested mode: an authorized verifier (the contract owner, representing an      off-chain validator or a Lit Action) calls {attestVerification}. Useful      where a verifier isn't deployed for the chain/provider.   3. Trust-on-submit mode (dev/demo only): when {autoVerifyOnSubmit} is      enabled, {submitProofHash} marks the caller verified on first hash. NOT a      cryptographic guarantee — disable in production.

OwnableInvalidOwner(address).details: The owner is not a valid owner account. (eg. `address(0)`)

OwnableUnauthorizedAccount(address).details: The caller account is not authorized to perform an operation.

attestVerification(address,bool).details: Restricted to the owner/verifier. This is the production path that gives `isVerified` real meaning, independent of {autoVerifyOnSubmit}.

params._status: True to mark verified, false to revoke.
params._user: The whistleblower whose status is being attested.

params._autoVerifyOnSubmit: Enable trust-on-submit verification (dev/demo). Set        false in production and use {attestVerification} instead.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

setReclaimVerifier(address).details: Owner-only. Set to a valid verifier on chains/providers Reclaim supports; leave as the zero address to disable the on-chain verification path.

params._verifier: Address of the Reclaim verifier contract (or address(0)).

params._proofHash: keccak256 hash of the serialized Reclaim proof JSON.

params.proof: The Reclaim proof, as produced by the JS SDK's `transformForOnchain`.

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

attestVerification(address,bool).notice: Authoritatively set a user's verified status after their proof has been validated off-chain (or by a Lit Action acting as the verifier).

autoVerifyOnSubmit().notice: When true, the first recorded proof hash trust-marks the user as verified without an explicit attestation. Convenience for dev/demo only.

getProofCount(address).notice: Get the number of proofs submitted by a user (reputation score proxy).

getProofHashes(address).notice: Get all proof hashes submitted by a user.

getRegisteredUserCount().notice: Get the total number of registered users.

isVerified(address).notice: Check if a user has verified status (at least one proof submitted).

reclaimVerifier().notice: Deployed Reclaim verifier used by {submitVerifiedProof}. When the zero address, on-chain proof verification is disabled (fall back to attestation / trust-on-submit).

registeredUsers(uint256).notice: Track all registered users for enumeration

setAutoVerifyOnSubmit(bool).notice: Toggle trust-on-submit verification. Should be disabled in production.

setReclaimVerifier(address).notice: Set (or clear) the deployed Reclaim verifier address.

setStealthMetaAddress(string).notice: Set or update the user's ERC-5564 stealth meta-address for anonymous payments.

submitProofHash(bytes32).notice: Submit a hash of a Reclaim zkTLS proof to build on-chain reputation. The full proof JSON is stored off-chain; only its keccak256 hash is recorded here.

submitVerifiedProof(((string,string,stri.notice: Submit a full Reclaim proof for trustless, on-chain verification. The proof's witness signatures are checked by the deployed Reclaim verifier; if they pass, the proof's `owner` is marked verified and the claim identifier is recorded. Verification accrues to `proof.signedClaim.claim.owner` (not the caller) so a valid proof cannot be replayed to verify a different account, and so it can be relayed (e.g. via a gasless sponsor) on the owner's behalf.

userdoc.notice: Stores hashes of Reclaim Protocol zkTLS proofs on-chain to establish whistleblower credibility without revealing identity. Journalists can verify that a source has cryptographic proof of employment/access by checking the proof hashes stored here against the off-chain JSON proofs.
